question: What directly accessible fish-survey evidence does the 2018 New Manila Reclamation EIS expose for its Pasig River freshwater-ecology stations, and can its detailed finfish tables be extracted from the public indexed copy?
citation: City Government of Manila. (2018). Environmental Impact Statement (EIS) Report: New Manila Reclamation Project, City of Manila. Official PDF hosted by the DENR Environmental Management Bureau EIA portal.

sourceAccess.accessMethod: Reviewed the official EMB-hosted searchable PDF text and its indexed table of contents on 2026-11-19. The December report copy exposes its table of contents and executive-summary text in the search index but not the body pages containing the listed finfish tables. A direct HEAD request to the official PDF returned HTTP 403; no access restriction was bypassed and no local copy retained.
sourceLocators: Executive Summary, Table ES-3, EIS page ES-7: fish biota methods report three Pasig River sampling stations surveyed July 23–24, 2018, with test fishing using cast net and hook-and-line.

Executive Summary, EIS page ES-14: three test-fishing operations are summarized as yielding six brackishwater fish species dominated by “Tilapia.” The summary does not name the other species or provide counts.

Table of Contents: Table 2-16 lists coordinates of actual-fishing (TSF) stations on report page 2-139; Figure 2-86 locates fish posts 2–4 as freshwater fish sampling stations and distinguishes fish post 1 as a marine-survey site (pages 2-140 to 2-141). Coordinates were not retrieved.

Table of Contents: Table 2-21, finfish diversity during actual-fishing documentation and key-informant interviews, report page 2-160; Table 2-22, diversity and catch per unit effort during actual-fishing documentation, page 2-161. The table contents were not retrieved.

Table of Contents also lists Table 2-29 as a separate Bacoor Bay marine-ecology fish table dated 2017 and Table 2-30 as a separate Baseco marine catch-landing table dated July 2018; neither table was reviewed or combined with the Pasig freshwater results.
sourceAccess.accessLimit: The searchable PDF extraction reaches its executive-summary and table-of-contents content but does not expose the report pages containing Tables 2-16, 2-21, or 2-22. The accessible source therefore verifies that detailed data tables exist, not their rows or values.

studyScope.localityContext: The EIS describes three freshwater-ecology sampling stations proximal to the BASECO Compound in the City of Manila.
studyScope.methodAsReported: Test fishing in the river with cast net and hook-and-line; executive summary describes three operations. Fish, crustaceans, and food-value macro-invertebrates were also subject to opportunistic in-situ identification in macrobenthos stations.
studyScope.resultAsReported: The executive summary says six brackishwater species were yielded and that “Tilapia” dominated.
studyScope.resultLimit: No species binomials, per-station taxa, catch totals, CPUE values, station coordinates, specimen vouchers, or key-informant attribution were recovered from the indexed body tables.

outOfScopeTables.sourceContext: Common fish species caught in Bacoor Bay during marine ecology baseline assessment, 2017-08-03
outOfScopeTables.decision: Not reviewed or merged with the Pasig River freshwater survey.

outOfScopeTables.sourceContext: Catch composition and CPUE documented during marine catch landing in Baseco, July 2018
outOfScopeTables.decision: Not reviewed or merged with the Pasig River freshwater survey.

decision.disposition: Catalog the EIS as a primary, historical source lead only. Preserve the executive-summary finding as source-level context and leave all species-level data untranscribed until the actual tables can be retrieved and reviewed.

limitations: The report is a project EIS baseline, not a systematic or current Pasig River inventory.
The executive summary gives a count of six species but omits their names and station-level details.
The table of contents alone cannot validate any species identity, abundance, CPUE, sampling coordinates, or key-informant statement.
The nominal field methods do not establish fishing access, present-day catchability, legal status, or food safety.
No item-specific republication license or permission was verified; no tables, maps, or species images are reproduced.
This EIS covers additional localities and marine surveys; the separate Bacoor Bay and Baseco marine tables are not evidence for the Pasig freshwater stations reviewed here.
nextActions: Seek a publicly accessible full-report copy or page images through an authorized public repository or direct source-provided access; do not circumvent the EMB access restriction.

If the table pages become available, verify Tables 2-16, 2-21, and 2-22 together, preserve source spellings and provenance, and compare the results against taxonomy and locality evidence before creating any occurrence candidates.
Keep this source research-only until exact taxon names, table rows, and applicable reuse terms are reviewed.
